stem.text: Selected values of a function f are given in the table. The function f is not defined at \( x = -3 \). What does the table suggest about \( \lim_{x \to -3} f(x) \)?

answer_key.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs keep alternating as x approaches -3.

worked_solution.text: On each side the outputs switch between 6 and -1 however close x comes to -3.
worked_solution.rule_named: reading a table from one side

worked_solution.text: The outputs do not settle toward any single value, so the table suggests the limit does not exist.
worked_solution.rule_named: limit requires the outputs to settle

options.label: The table suggests that the limit is 6, because the outputs keep returning to 6.
options.derivation: one of the two values the outputs alternate between reported as the limit

options.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because no limit can exist where f is not defined, as at x = -3.
options.derivation: nonexistence concluded from f being undefined at the target rather than from the outputs

options.label: The table suggests that the limit does not exist, because the outputs keep alternating as x approaches -3.
